title: Stochastic guiding-center dust
text:
Extension of guiding-center and kinetic ideas to highly charged dust in MHD turbulence, with a stochastic formulation suited to coupling small-scale grain physics to large-scale ISM models.
Manuscript: (Moseley, Eric R., et al. in prep.) (with R. Teyssier and S. E. Clark). When a preprint exists, add the arXiv/DOI link and a schematic figure.

title: MHD-PIC dust in RAMSES
text:
Dust dynamics in RAMSES — Part I (Moseley et al. 2023) and Part II (Moseley and Teyssier 2025). MHD-PIC implementation and turbulent-box experiments for charged grains.
Code: RAMSES.

title: Itô tracers for Eulerian hydrodynamics
text:
Stochastic tracer particles whose statistics are tied to the numerical flux of the underlying finite-volume scheme, for passive scalars and related applications in RAMSES / mini-RAMSES.
Published preprint: arXiv:2604.23041 — (Moseley et al. 2026).
When you add figure panels from the paper, place images under assets/img/ and embed them here with Markdown ![]().

title: Eric R. Moseley
text:
Kavli Institute for Particle Astrophysics and Cosmology
Stanford, CA
I am a KIPAC Fellow at Stanford and SLAC. I work on numerical methods for astrophysical fluids, non-ideal MHD, interstellar chemistry, magnetic field structure, dust–gas dynamics and instabilities, and cosmic-ray propagation, diffusion, and confinement—often with MHD particle-in-cell methods in RAMSES.
My first-author series on dust in RAMSES covers methods and turbulent acceleration (Moseley et al. 2023) and equilibrium drift distributions of charged grains (Moseley and Teyssier 2025), building on earlier work on the CNM (Moseley et al. 2021) and resonant drag instabilities (Moseley et al. 2019). Itô tracers—continuous-trajectory Lagrangian particles matched to Eulerian hydrodynamics—are public as (Moseley et al. 2026). I am also preparing a stochastic guiding-center formulation for highly charged dust (Moseley, Eric R., et al. in prep.).
I received my Ph.D. and M.A. in astrophysics from Princeton University (2024 and 2020) and my B.S. from Caltech (2018). Full lists: Publications, Google Scholar, ORCID.
